key_findings.finding: Direct human in-vitro evidence supports the conclusion that EphB4 activation reduces neointimal hyperplasia: discarded human saphenous-vein rings were cultured for 14 days with ephrin-B2/Fc (2 μg/mL), which reduced the neointima/media ratio from 0.726 ± 0.142 in untreated cultured veins to 0.630 ± 0.132 (matched n=19, P=.017; baseline 0.456 ± 0.097).

source_tools.relevance: Full abstract and results preview of the direct experimental study

key_findings.finding: The activating manipulation was exogenous clustered ephrin-B2/Fc, used as a ligand agonist of EphB4; the study additionally showed EphB4 phosphorylation in saphenous-vein endothelium after adventitial ephrin-B2/Fc delivery during arterial shear stress, supporting on-target receptor activation.

source_tools.relevance: Methods, results, and conclusions of the direct human saphenous-vein study

key_findings.finding: Related mechanistic readouts were obtained in primary human umbilical-vein endothelial cells rather than saphenous-vein smooth-muscle cells: ephrin-B2/Fc stimulated Akt, eNOS, and caveolin-1 phosphorylation and increased nitric-oxide release. The reported human saphenous-vein endpoint was neointimal thickness/ratio; the abstract does not report a direct smooth-muscle migration or proliferation assay in saphenous-vein tissue.

key_findings.finding: The evidence should not be conflated with EphB4 inhibition or with non-human/in-vivo work: the same paper cites prior murine vein-graft experiments, but its positive human result is organ culture of human saphenous-vein rings; the searched literature did not identify a competing direct human saphenous-vein organ-culture study using EphB4 inhibition. Ephrin-B2 is the activating ligand/manipulation here, not an EphB4 inhibitor.
